questions.prompt: Which describes authentication (as opposed to authorization)?

options.text: Deciding what actions an identity is allowed to perform
Proving who you are, usually by signing in
Billing your usage to a subscription

questions.explanation: Authentication answers 'who are you?' (proving identity by signing in). Authorization answers 'what may you do?' — that's RBAC.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID is the current name for Azure Active Directory
An RBAC role assignment combines a principal, a role, and a scope
Role assignments inherit downward through the hierarchy
Entra ID is identical to on-premises Active Directory Domain Services

questions.explanation: Entra ID is the renamed Azure AD; RBAC = principal + role + scope, inheriting downward. Entra ID is NOT the same as on-premises AD DS (no OUs/Group Policy/domain join).

questions.prompt: Requiring two or more proofs of identity at sign-in (like a password plus a phone app) is abbreviated ____.
questions.explanation: MFA (multifactor authentication) requires two or more verification factors and blocks the vast majority of password-based attacks.

questions.prompt: Order these built-in roles from LEAST to MOST access.
questions.explanation: Reader can only view; Contributor can manage resources but not grant access; Owner has full access including managing others' access.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Full access including managing others' access
Manage resources but not grant access to others
Grant only the minimum access needed

questions.explanation: Owner is full control; Contributor manages resources but not access; Reader is view-only; least privilege grants the minimum necessary.
